User_Location_Alignment.evidence: carried as written; USER_041 is already at LOC_003, so the five-user set holds once the other four move

notes: Merged from two independent passes that agree on the six CIs, the three alerts (selected by incident and recipient, since the request fixes no sending order), the other-New-York stay and all four dispositions. disagreement: A's stay that USER_041's three other CIs (CI_010, CI_011, CI_098) stay at LOC_001 (B had no such requirement); kept because it is the boundary of the owner-alignment selector: an agent that relocates the impacted owners together with their assets would sweep in the only CIs the five owners hold outside the Sales Office. disagreement: value: the owner requirement's set and count (A five users, expected 5, seed_count 1; B four, expected 4, seed_count 0); A's kept as the tighter predicate that also carries the original check as written. disagreement: form: the LOC_002 users stay excludes five users in A and four in B; the same seven rows on the seed, so the five-user list is kept to match the owner requirement. The passes list the six CIs in different orders; the original check's order is kept. The CMDB audit and the transfer plan are prose with no table. INC_030 reaches CI_006 only through incident.configuration_item; no listed tool searches incidents by CI, so agents that follow the tools will miss it, but the request's 'associated' covers it. Least sure: keeping the USER_041 CI stay, which sits at the edge of the stay rule (a boundary, not a generic invariant, only if an owner-based reading counts as a loose reading of 'associated with the Sales Office location').
